requirements.requirement: Convert the staged Latin-1 filenames into valid UTF-8 filenames under converted/, retaining directory structure and file contents.
requirements.summary: The two non-colliding Latin-1 names were mapped to café.txt and résumé.txt. Pre- and post-restart verification directly confirms valid UTF-8 destination names, an exact three-entry destination tree, and content hashes matching the corresponding sources. The staged tree was flat, so its directory structure was retained.
Final verification finds exactly the three original raw filename byte sequences in imported/, with unchanged file hashes, modes, owners, and groups. The inventory hash also remains unchanged.

requirements.requirement: Report any existing UTF-8 destination collision without overwriting the destination or silently dropping the source.
requirements.summary: plain.txt was detected as a collision and recorded in conversion-report.tsv with both hashes. The existing destination retained its original hash, the distinct source remained present, and the report survived restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after execution, node1 remained RHEL 10.0 on kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64. Conversion used the installed RHEL-packaged Python runtime; the lifecycle package-health checks remained successful and no package installation or upgrade appears in the command timeline.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct and coherent before, after, and post-restart evidence. The imported tree was preserved, the two available Latin-1 names were converted with matching contents, the pre-existing plain.txt collision was preserved and reported, and the operating-system release and kernel were unchanged. The mandatory node1 restart protocol is complete and independently corroborated by lifecycle observations.
